title: Rational sections and elementary divisor modifications on a regular curve
statement:
Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian regular scheme of dimension one [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-dimension], where Noetherian means quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian, with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field]. For each closed point $x$, let $v_x:K^*\to\mathbf Z$ be the normalized valuation of the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Here $v_x(f)=n$ means $f=u t^n$ for a unit $u\in\mathcal O_{X,x}^*$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; $\kappa(x)$ denotes the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Tensor products are those of module sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A divisor means a finite formal sum $D=\sum_xn_x[x]$. Define $\mathcal O_X(D)$ as the subsheaf of the constant rational-function sheaf $K$ whose sections on a nonempty open $U$ are $0$ and the $f\in K^*$ with $v_x(f)+n_x\geq0$ for all closed $x\in U$.
(1) $\mathcal O_X(D)$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], $\mathcal O_X(0)=\mathcal O_X$, and multiplication gives $\mathcal O_X(D)\otimes\mathcal O_X(E)\simeq\mathcal O_X(D+E)$.
(2) If $\mathcal L$ is invertible and $0\ne s\in\mathcal L_\eta$, write $s=f_xe_x$ for a local generator at $x$. The integers $v_x(f_x)$ are independent of that generator and vanish except at finitely many $x$. Put $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_xv_x(f_x)[x]$. Multiplication by $s$ gives $\mathcal O_X(\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s))\simeq\mathcal L$. Such an $s$ always exists. If $s$ is a nonzero global section, its divisor is effective. For $f\in K^*$, $\mathcal O_X(\operatorname{div}(f))\simeq\mathcal O_X$.
(3) For any divisor $D$ and closed point $x$, the natural inclusion fits into a short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal O_X(D-[x])\to\mathcal O_X(D)\to i_{x,*}V\to0$, where $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ and $V$ is a one-dimensional $\kappa(x)$-vector space (hence the last sheaf is noncanonically isomorphic to $i_{x,*}\kappa(x)$).
